gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-georama: Playful and a little bossy, Early GameBoy stretches its spacing wide under a skyward x-height line. Georama takes over below with a bracelet-open c and barely rising capitals, so the sans-serif text stays out of its way.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-gidole: Gidole reads like neon tubing, each stroke holding its width however it turns, with a high-set midline and open terminals. Early GameBoy swells and thins gently above it, wide and playful.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-golos-text: Golos Text has a widely parted s and an x-height that fills the line, every letter wire-bent at one stroke width. Golos Text handles the reading, while Early GameBoy brings the etched-glass swagger.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-hedvig-lette: Hedvig Letters Sans stands tall, with a clear gap where the c ends. Early GameBoy is the one for commanding, playful display lettering, while the body face just gets on with being approachable.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-heebo: Commanding and a little playful, Early GameBoy spaces its letters wide with a modest swing in stroke weight. Heebo can stay at a modest size, since its tall central band and stopped-short curves carry the reading.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-hind-madurai: A skyward x-height line gives Early GameBoy its lift. It handles the loud, wide-spaced heading work, while Hind Madurai handles the text with ribbon-cut stroke ends and lowercase that fills the line.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-hind-mysuru: Playful and wide-spaced, Early GameBoy leads. Hind Mysuru backs it with single-stroke brush lines, lowercase tops pressing toward the ascenders, so the text stays steady under the heading's faint nib pressure.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-hind-siligur: Early GameBoy stretches out wide and means it. Hind Siliguri hums along beneath in flat, constant line weight, its gapped rounds giving the heading's heavier stems something quiet to push against.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-hind-vadodar: Commanding and playful, Early GameBoy spaces its letters wide, with slight but noticeable stroke contrast. And Hind Vadodara reads smoothly once the text runs on, its spacious terminal gaps and tall bowls keeping each line open.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-huninn: Extended, open tracking is the first thing Early GameBoy shows, softened by hand-inked modulation. And what holds it together is Huninn, a sans-serif whose strokes never vary in thickness, crossbars included.
